description: A department head must choose the recipient of an annual collaboration award and finalize how the recognition will be delivered, including the supporting record and the recipient's participation in related public events.

shared_context.S1: The department's annual collaboration award has two finalists: Jules and Casey.
shared_context.S2: The award recognizes sustained work that improves cooperation across teams.
shared_context.S3: The standard recognition package includes a public announcement, a five-minute spotlight at the department meeting, and an invitation to represent the department on an external collaboration panel.
shared_context.S4: Helena makes the binding award decision and finalizes the recognition package.
shared_context.S5: The department's award review meeting includes a brief round for project colleagues and event staff to share relevant input before the decision is recorded.
shared_context.S6: The review procedure requires each participant with relevant input to make a formal disclosure during that input round, and Helena records each formal disclosure before settling the award and recognition package.

PF1.text: Malcolm personally observed Jules lead exactly six listening sessions between the product and support teams after repeated handoff tensions; the sessions produced a shared escalation practice that both teams still use. Malcolm has not put this in the nomination record because he expected Jules's project lead to document it.

PF2.text: Jules told Sofia in confidence that a caregiving appointment conflicts with the award meeting in nine days and that Jules cannot appear live or represent the department on the external collaboration panel; Jules asked for a written announcement instead and asked Sofia not to raise the request until the finalists were reviewed.

revealed: fact_id formally disclosed aloud during the review

acceptance_conditions: Jules must receive the collaboration award.
The award record must state that Jules led exactly six listening sessions.
The award record must state that those sessions produced the shared escalation practice.
Recognition must be delivered through a written announcement with no live spotlight.
Jules must not be assigned to represent the department on the external collaboration panel.
A recognition-package-adjustment commitment for Jules must be logged.

content_checks.C4: decisions['recognition_mode'] in ['written announcement', 'written announcement in place of live spotlight']
content_checks.C6: any(c['target'] == 'Jules' and c['type'] in ['recognition_package', 'recognition_package_adjustment', 'recognition_adjustment', 'recognition_package_adaptation', 'written_announcement', 'accommodate scheduling constraint'] for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed
provenance_checks.P2: 'PF2' in credited_facts and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: Knowing that Jules led exactly six listening sessions and created the still-used shared escalation practice changes the recipient to Jules and changes the award record to six sessions with that practice.

Knowing that Jules cannot attend live or represent the department changes recognition_mode to a written announcement, changes external_panel_representation to false, and requires a recognition-package commitment for Jules.
